back: Software that creates, stores, secures and gives controlled access to a database for many users.
Data about the data: field names, types, sizes, validation rules, keys and relationships.
The design of the whole database: tables, fields, data types, keys and relationships, not the physical storage.
Validation rules, primary key rules and referential integrity keep the data correct and consistent.
Permissions (none, read, read and write) set for each user or group on each table.
Full backups copy everything; incremental backups copy only the changes. The database is restored after a failure.
The part of the DBMS that checks and carries out a query and returns the result.
The tools used to create tables, validation rules, forms, reports and queries.
DDL (CREATE TABLE, ALTER TABLE) defines the structure. DML (SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE) works with the data.
